title: Site header and logo placement
when: The user wants a site header designed: where the logo goes, how big, how nav and actions line up, sticky or not.
inputs: nav links and the one header action
prompt:
Goal: A compact header with the logo linking home on the left and nav plus one action aligned on one line, adapting to phones.
Steps:
1. Logo top left inside a link to the home page, with the site name as its accessible text (img alt, or visually hidden text beside an svg).
2. Size the logo by height: 28 to 40 px on desktop, 24 to 32 px on phones, with width and height attributes.
3. Layout: flex, align-items: center, justify-content: space-between, gap var(--space-5), height 56 to 72 px.
4. Order: logo, primary nav, one header action (Book now); on narrow screens collapse the nav first and keep the action.
5. If sticky: position: sticky; top: 0, a solid background, and scroll-padding-top on html equal to the header height.
6. Make a skip link the first focusable element, pointing at main.
Quality bar:
- Logo legible and never stretched.
- Header under 12 percent of a phone screen.
- Nav items centered on the logo line.
Pitfalls:
- Giant logos that push content down.
- A logo that does not link home.
- Transparent sticky headers over busy content.
Verify:
- [ ] The logo link goes home with a text name.
- [ ] Logo img has alt, width and height.
- [ ] Navigation sits in a nav.
- [ ] A skip link targets main.
Output: The header markup on every page and header rules in style.css.

examples.input: onde coloco a logo e o menu no topo do site
examples.output: logo 32px tall linking home on the left, nav in the middle, Book now on the right, sticky with solid background
